card: Suppresses transmitting the response body for HTTP HEAD requests in the internal HTTP server, complying with RFC 9110 section 9.3.2. Previously, HEAD responses sent the full response body along with headers, leaving unread bytes on keep-alive connections that could desynchronize or corrupt subsequent responses when operating behind connection-pooling reverse proxies like nginx. Both REST endpoints and unauthenticated RPC 405 paths are affected without requiring credentials. Functional tests verify that raw socket requests receive correct Content-Length headers with no following payload bytes.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the patch; previous description accurately reflects the current commits and diff.
evidence: PR description demonstrates that a raw HEAD request returns 'JSONRPC server handles only POST requests' body bytes after headers with a Content-Length header: 'A client that follows the specification stops reading after the header section, so the body bytes stay on the connection and are read as the start of the next response.'
PR description notes exposure: 'Both the 405 reply of the RPC endpoint and the REST endpoints answer HEAD without authentication, so a client that is merely allowed to connect can trigger it.'
problem: The HTTP server transmits body bytes in response to HEAD requests. Because RFC-compliant clients stop reading at the header terminator, the unconsumed body bytes remain in the connection buffer and are parsed as the beginning of the next HTTP response, desynchronizing pipelined or pooled keepalive connections behind reverse proxies like nginx.

risk.why: A mistake in HTTP frame formatting or keepalive handling could break communication with RPC or REST clients and reverse proxies.

summary: Suppresses the response body when replying to HTTP HEAD requests while leaving the response headers (including Content-Length) unchanged. Per RFC 9110, HEAD responses must reflect the headers of an equivalent GET response without transmitting payload bytes. Accompanying functional tests verify raw socket behavior across RPC (405 error response) and REST (200 success response) endpoints.
